title: Gas chromatography method to quantify α-monobenzoate glycerol in methanolic solutions using methyl benzoate as internal standard and a Rxi-1ms column
author: de Macedo
materials: Methanol (>99.9%, liquid, HPLC grade), glycerol (99.5%, liquid), benzoic acid (99.5%, solid), and methyl benzoate (99%, liquid), were purchased from Sigma-Aldrich and used as received. Except the benzoic acid which was ground using an agate mortar and pestle before its use. The α-monobenzoate glycerol (1 g; 95%, pasty-like solid) was purchased from BLD Pharm China.
resulted in the chromatograms shown in Fig.

steps.title: Gather reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Obtain methanol (≥99.9 % HPLC grade), glycerol (99.5 %), benzoic acid (99.5 %) and methyl benzoate (99 %) from Sigma‑Aldrich; grind benzoic acid with an agate mortar and pestle; obtain α‑monobenzoate glycerol (α‑MBG, 1 g, 95 %); prepare a Hamilton glass microliter syringe (model 701) and a Labmate HTL 1000 µL micropipette; have ready 25 mL volumetric flasks, glass vials with PTFE‑lined septa, and the Shimadzu GC‑QP2010Plus equipped with a flame‑ionization detector and an Rxi‑1ms column (29.8 m × 0.25 mm i.d. × 25 µm film).

steps.title: Prepare four calibration mixtures
steps.instruction: For each mixture (1–4) weigh the appropriate amount of α‑MBG into a 25 mL volumetric flask, add methyl benzoate (MBe) as internal standard with the Labmate HTL micropipette to reach 0.10 mol L⁻¹ MBe, then fill to the mark with methanol; mix and transfer the solution to a glass vial with a PTFE‑lined septum.

substeps.instruction: Mixture 1: α‑MBG 0.0005 mol L⁻¹, MBe 0.10 mol L⁻¹.
Mixture 2: α‑MBG 0.00075 mol L⁻¹, MBe 0.10 mol L⁻¹.
Mixture 3: α‑MBG 0.001 mol L⁻¹, MBe 0.10 mol L⁻¹.
Mixture 4: α‑MBG 0.00125 mol L⁻¹, MBe 0.10 mol L⁻¹.

steps.title: Set GC‑MS instrument parameters
steps.instruction: Install the Rxi‑1ms column, select high‑purity helium as carrier gas, and program the instrument exactly as shown in Table 2.

substeps.instruction: SetRate (°C min⁻¹) – Final Temperature (°C) – Hold time (min)
Use a Hamilton glass microliter syringe (model 701) for manual injection; inject approximately 1 µL per run; raise the piston slowly to avoid air bubbles.

steps.title: Run blank and methanol test
steps.instruction: Perform a blank run (no injection) to check for anomalous peaks, then inject 1 µL of pure methanol to verify its purity and retention time (< 3 min); set a cutting solvent time of 3 min to exclude the methanol peak from subsequent analyses.

steps.title: Inject calibration mixtures in triplicate
steps.instruction: For each of the four calibration mixtures, inject 1 µL into the GC‑MS three times, using the slow‑piston technique, and record the chromatograms.

steps.title: Determine peak parameters
steps.instruction: Using GCMS Postrun software (Version 4.45), obtain start time (ST), end time (ET), retention time (RT) and peak area for MBe (ST 8.379 ± 0.01 min, ET 8.386 ± 0.01 min, RT 8.382 ± 0.01 min) and for α‑MBG (ST 16.096 ± 0.00 min, ET 16.102 ± 0.01 min, RT 16.099 ± 0.01 min); calculate the area ratio Areaα‑MBG / AreaMBe for each injection.

steps.title: Construct calibration curve
steps.instruction: Enter the average area ratios for each mixture (Table 3) and the corresponding α‑MBG concentrations (Table 1) into Origin PRO, perform a linear fit, and record the slope (0.03455) and intercept (5.01645 × 10⁻⁵). The calibration equation is Cα‑MBG = 0.03455 × (Areaα‑MBG / AreaMBe) + 5.01645 × 10⁻⁵ mol L⁻¹.

steps.title: Analyze unknown sample (optional)
steps.instruction: Prepare a methanolic solution containing glycerol, benzoic acid and MBe (and possibly α‑MBG); inject 1 µL under the same conditions; verify the MBe peak at ~8.38 min and the α‑MBG peak at ~16.10 min; if a slight overlap occurs near the glycerol end time and MBe start time, re‑inject, shake the vial, or dilute the sample before the next injection to improve resolution.
